$comment: The external binaries the photo and encoding pipelines shell out to, declared
once so `bun run tools:check` can verify them. NOT in infra.json on purpose:
that file declares Cloudflare and GitHub state and `infra:check` diffs it
against those APIs, while nothing here is remote and nothing here has an API.
Mixing them would give one file two unrelated contracts.
This exists because the list used to live in three places that disagreed:
CLAUDE.md's encoder section, MAINTENANCE.md's brew line, and inline guards in
the scripts. ffmpeg, cwebp, ssimulacra2 and butteraugli_main were required and
documented nowhere, so a clean machine met them as a raw shell error.
`optional` means a script degrades rather than exits: avifenc falls back to
sips in add-photos.sh and reencode-thumbnails.sh, and is REQUIRED by the two
encoding-grid scripts, so it is listed optional and its hard callers are named
in `required_by` anyway. A tool that is optional everywhere is still declared,
because the point is a complete list rather than a blocking one.
`path` is for a binary a script resolves by absolute location rather than
PATH. jpegtran is the only one: mozjpeg is keg-only, so `command -v jpegtran`
can find libjpeg-turbo's copy while the scripts use mozjpeg's, and probing
PATH would report a pass on the wrong binary.
`version` is how to ASK a binary what it is, per tool, because there is no
convention: exif-sooc answers `exif-sooc 0.2.0`, jq answers `jq-1.7.1-apple`,
sips answers `sips-316`, avifenc answers `Version: 1.4.2 (...)`, cwebp answers
a bare `1.6.0`, and mozjpeg's two answer `mozjpeg version 4.1.5 (build ...)` on
stderr. Two of them answer nothing at all, so they say so rather than being
quietly skipped.
A `match` may capture SEVERAL components, as NAMED groups, and it has to
wherever the binary's own version is not what decides the bytes. avifenc is
the wrapper over aom, and brew can relink it against a newer aom without
moving libavif's 1.4.2, so reading 1.4.2 alone passes through exactly the
drift this tier exists to catch; aom 3.13 already changed the still-image
tune default. zenc is the same shape one layer in, since its own 0.1.0 has
never moved while dependabot bumps the zenjpeg pin underneath it. Named
groups join into the recorded string as `name value, name value`, so the
names are part of what is compared rather than documentation nobody reads.
A multi-part pattern may NOT carry a `min_version`: the ordering compares one
number per component and would silently stop flooring, so check-tools.ts
fails on the pair instead.
`bytes` marks a tool whose version decides SHIPPED BYTES, and `recorded` is the
version that made the ones committed today. That pairing is the point of this
block: /i/ is content-addressed, so re-encoding under a different encoder mints
new URLs, orphans every a-dict snapshot naming the old hash, and (gotcha 41) can
leave derived data like the histograms describing pixels nobody serves. So the
question worth asking here is whether the avifenc on this machine is the one
that baked the library. Whether a newer one exists is brew's job, and brew
already answers it.
`recorded` is a BASELINE OBSERVED ON 2026-08-24, not a reconstruction. Nothing
recorded which encoder made the 632 files in public/i, and #394 re-encoded 316
of them on 2026-08-14, so claiming these versions produced them would be
inventing provenance. What is true is that they are the versions the next run
will use, and that a future re-encode updates them. It becomes a real record
going forward rather than being one already.

tools.why: every EXIF read and write in the pipeline. It emits metadata.json's record shape directly and owns the merge, which retired the 50-line jq reshape and build-recipes.py, and on 2026-08-14 it took the last of exiftool's jobs too: orientation reads, -all= strips and -TagsFromFile copies, in ExifTool's own flag spellings. Pinned at 0.2.0 by the guards in the writing scripts: 0.1.0 could not write, and its -all= truncated progressive JPEGs at the first scan, which is every JPEG this pipeline produces
JSON assembly in the metadata shell scripts
tools.bytes_why: assembles JSON, so its output is the same text at any version

tools.why: resize, HEIF decode, and the AVIF fallback encoder
pulls the R2 originals back down
tools.bytes_why: moves bytes it did not make

tools.why: builds zenc, the shipped JPEG encoder, on first run
tools.bytes_why: builds zenc, and zenjpeg's encode is deterministic for a given pin, which dependabot owns in tools/photos/zenc/Cargo.toml. A compiler bump does not move a JPEG

tools.why: the JPEG encoder for every shipped tier, plus the square/resize geometry and the histogram bake. It decides the bytes of the JPG half of /i/ exactly the way avifenc decides the AVIF half, and it was the one encoder here with no entry: `cargo` was declared as its BUILD prerequisite, which is a different question from which encoder baked the library
tools.optional_why: `optional` here means BUILT ON DEMAND rather than degrades: every caller runs `cargo build --release` when the binary is missing, so an absent zenc on a fresh checkout is a state the pipeline repairs itself rather than a prerequisite anybody has to go install. A missing `cargo` is the blocking failure, and cargo is declared above

tools.why: progressive rearrangement of the R2 share copies, a coefficient reorder. It did EXIF-orientation rotation until 2026-08-26; that is `zenc square --orient` now, per CLAUDE.md gotcha 3
the chroma-subsampling row of the /garage/encoding grids

the encoder-comparison grids on /garage/encoding. The PHOTO PIPELINE no longer reaches for this one: add-photos and reencode-thumbnails prefer tools/photos/libavif/build/avifenc, a pinned from-source build, and fall back here and then to sips
tools.bytes_why: it still bakes the /garage/encoding sample bytes and the public/cars reference pair. It no longer bakes /i/: that moved to the pinned build, whose version is fixed by LIBAVIF_TAG in tools/photos/libavif/build.sh rather than recorded here, because a pin does not drift and this entry's `recorded` field exists only to catch drift in an ambient brew install

tools.why: the WebP point on the /garage/encoding format grid
tools.bytes_why: it still bakes the /garage/encoding sample bytes. It no longer bakes /i/: that moved to the pinned build, whose version is fixed by LIBAVIF_TAG in tools/photos/libavif/build.sh rather than recorded here, because a pin does not drift and this entry's `recorded` field exists only to catch drift in an ambient brew install

tools.why: PNG to PPM, because cjpeg will not read PNG and sips BMP confuses it; also the independent reduction the one-step probe scores against

tools.install: build libjxl with -DJPEGXL_ENABLE_TOOLS=ON; brew's jpeg-xl does not ship it
tools.why: the perceptual metric the Instagram export searches quality against, and the one the one-step ingest probe compares geometries with

version.why: a libjxl tool: it takes no version flag and prints usage instead. It is a METRIC rather than an encoder, so it never touches a shipped byte, and the build that produced it is the only record there is

tools.install: build libjxl with -DJPEGXL_ENABLE_TOOLS=ON; brew's jpeg-xl does not ship it
tools.why: the second metric bounding that same search

version.why: the same libjxl build, the same absence, and the same reason it does not matter: it bounds a quality search rather than encoding anything

tools.why: alt text in add-photos.sh, plus gen-pixel-peeper.py; only the last of those wants Pillow, from tools/photos/requirements.txt. build-recipes.py was the third consumer and was deleted on 2026-08-14 when exif-sooc took over the recipe card
tools.bytes_why: captions and one study-page generator. What would move those is Pillow, which tools/photos/requirements.txt pins and dependabot owns
